selection: Natural terminal lakes that ADR-112 permits as a separate water type: a closed basin with no dam and no engineered full pool, an owner-operated daily series of surface elevation with its datum named, and a reviewed waterbody point that resolves to exactly one NHDPlus HR waterbody at the project's 100-metre tolerance. A volume is published where the survey publishes a daily series on a named elevation-volume relation; without one, the entry says why in volume_finding and publishes the elevation alone (ADR-159). A lake whose parts are measured apart is listed by arm, each arm with its own site, point and elevation, and no combined level (ADR-159). No capacity, percent full, dam point or reservoir-rollup membership is recorded for any lake here, and a restoration or regulatory level is only ever a named target with its authority, decision, date and datum. Walker Lake was the first admission and Great Salt Lake the second; the candidates still held are in the withheld block with their findings.
keyed_by: usgs_site_no, or the lake's own key for a lake measured by arm (each arm names its site)

point.source: USGS monitoring location USGS-10288500, WALKER LAKE NR HAWTHORNE, NV, in decimal degrees on NAD83 (the site record's coordinate datum is NAD27; the decimal coordinates are the survey's NAD83 conversion)

waterbody.note: The site point resolves to exactly one NHDPlus HR waterbody within 100 metres, and Esri's USA Detailed Water Bodies names the same lake -- the probe's strongest outcome (ADR-106). The point is a gauge on the shore and stands for the whole lake; no outlet or dam point exists to record.

closed_basin.evidence: The Walker River ends in the lake and water leaves the basin by evaporation; the lake has no outlet (Lopes and Smith, 2007, SIR 2007-5012). The committed west-huc8 geometry places the site point in subbasin 16050304 Walker Lake inside basin 160503 Walker, and the survey's own hydrologic unit for the site agrees. The assignment is made from the published lake point, never from a synthetic outlet (ADR-112).

elevation.note: Reservoir elevation, the daily observation at 24:00, in feet above the site's vertical datum. The survey records the datum as NGVD29 with a site altitude of 3,900 feet. An elevation is published as a level and never as a percentage of any datum (ADR-112).

relation.name: Lopes and Smith (2007), Bathymetry of Walker Lake, West-Central Nevada, U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2007-5012
relation.note: The survey computes storage from the lake stage with this relation from 1 October 2014; the relation used before that date was Rush (1970). Recorded from ADR-112's review of 2026-09-04; the water-year summaries that state the change were not reachable on 2026-09-06. The published record starts on 2015-01-01, inside the current relation, so every published volume is on one relation and no reading is recomputed or repaired.

great-salt-lake.name: Great Salt Lake

waterbody.note: Each arm's site point resolves to exactly one NHDPlus HR waterbody within 100 metres, and it is the same one for both arms: NHDPlus HR draws Great Salt Lake as one LakePond polygon across the railroad causeway. Esri's USA Detailed Water Bodies names Great Salt Lake at both points. The one polygon is why the lake is published by arm and not by waterbody: the arms are measured apart and stand at different levels (ADR-159).

closed_basin.evidence: The survey's Utah Water Science Center describes Great Salt Lake as a terminal lake with no outlet to the sea (https://www.usgs.gov/centers/utah-water-science-center/science/great-salt-lake-elevations-and-areal-extent, checked 2026-11-11). The committed west-huc8 geometry places both arm points in subbasin 16020310 Great Salt Lake inside basin 160203 Great Salt Lake, and the survey's own hydrologic unit for both sites (160203100200) agrees. The assignment is made from the published arm points, never from a synthetic outlet (ADR-112).

arms.name: South Arm

point.source: USGS monitoring location USGS-10010000, GREAT SALT LAKE AT SALTAIR BOAT HARBOR, UT, in decimal degrees on NAD83 (the site record's coordinate datum is NAD27; the decimal coordinates are the survey's NAD83 conversion). The survey's Utah Water Science Center names this gauge, in the Saltair Boat Harbor at the southern end of the lake, as the record of the south part of the lake, which the Union Pacific Railroad causeway (1959) divides from the north part.

elevation.note: Lake water surface elevation above NGVD 1929, the daily mean, in feet. The datum is named by the parameter itself (62614 is the NGVD29 elevation; 62615 would be NAVD88), and the site record's vertical datum is NGVD29 with a gauge altitude of 4,186.8 feet. A level is published as a level and never as a percentage of anything (ADR-112).

arms.volume_finding: The survey publishes no daily volume series at this site: the time-series catalog lists elevation (62614) only. Its area-and-volume tables for the south arm are a published relation, but computing a volume from them is a method this project has not reviewed, so the arm publishes its elevation alone (ADR-159).

arms.name: North Arm

point.source: USGS monitoring location USGS-10010100, GREAT SALT LAKE NEAR SALINE, UT, in decimal degrees on NAD83 (the site record's coordinate datum is NAD27; the decimal coordinates are the survey's NAD83 conversion). The survey's Utah Water Science Center names this gauge as the record of the north part of the lake since April 1966, north of the Union Pacific Railroad causeway (1959).

elevation.note: Lake water surface elevation above NGVD 1929, the daily mean, in feet. The datum is named by the parameter itself, and the site record's vertical datum is NGVD29 with a gauge altitude of 4,189.8 feet. A level is published as a level and never as a percentage of anything (ADR-112).

arms.volume_finding: The survey publishes no daily volume series at this site: the time-series catalog lists elevation (62614) only. Its area-and-volume tables for the north arm are a published relation, but computing a volume from them is a method this project has not reviewed, so the arm publishes its elevation alone (ADR-159).

great-salt-lake.volume_finding: No combined volume: the survey publishes no daily volume series for the whole lake or for either arm. Its Utah Water Science Center publishes elevation-area-volume relationships for the lake and for each arm, but computing a volume from them is a method this project has not reviewed (ADR-159).

withheld.Pyramid Lake: Held for its update schedule, not its volume. The survey publishes the level at USGS-10336500, PYRAMID LAKE NR NIXON, NV, as parameter 00062 in feet above NGVD29 (the site record's vertical datum, altitude 3,940.29 feet), current to 2026-11-02 -- but only as discrete readings about once a month (statistic 00011; 23 readings from 2024-11-01 to 2026-11-02, none between 2025-09-03 and 2025-12-01), and the daily collection holds no series for the site (both checked 2026-11-11). ADR-159 makes the volume optional, so the missing volume relation no longer holds the lake. This roster and its freshness rule are daily (a reading is late after 2 days), and a monthly level needs its own update schedule, fetch path and late threshold, which is a decision of its own. The only other survey sites at the lake are two sediment-core sites with no series. This project's western source review (docs/WESTERN-SOURCE-CANDIDATES.md) recorded the Natural Resources Conservation Service's listing for the lake as monthly and semimonthly only.
withheld.Mono Lake: Held for its elevation series; its target is confirmed. The State Water Resources Control Board's Mono Lake page (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/waterrights/water_issues/programs/mono_lake/, checked 2026-11-11) states that Decision 1631, adopted in 1994, set a long-term management level of 6,392 feet above sea level, with a transition level of 6,391 feet; the decision text is linked there as wrd1631.pdf. No current, citable daily elevation series was found: USGS-10287000, MONO LK NR MONO LAKE CA, lists no time series in the survey's catalog; the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power's daily Mono Basin operations report (https://wsoweb.ladwp.com/aqueduct/operations/monobasin.htm) showed the lake elevation as n/a with no read date on 2026-11-11, on its own datum ('add 0.4 ft for USGS datum'), with no data file; and the Mono Lake Committee's lake-level page could not be read on 2026-11-11 (it refused the request), so its record is unreviewed. Held until a current daily elevation series with a stated datum is reviewed, and until the target's 'above sea level' is tied to that series' datum so the gap can be published in feet.
